subject: Wrapped-key exportability proof & secure key wipe for Acme SIG
messages:
From: Paul Moss <paul.moss@acme.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: Proof that wrapped-key exports are non-exportable + wipe logs

Hi Chloe,

As part of our SIG review, we need evidence that Redwood does not provide a mechanism to export unwrapped tenant keys (i.e., keys are always wrapped by a hardware-backed KEK/HSM and any export operation only yields wrapped material). Specifically we're looking for:

- A short attestation describing whether wrapped keys can be exported in plaintext under any supported workflow.
- Logs showing a recent rotation and subsequent secure erase of ephemeral wrapping keys (we expect rotation + wipe audit trail).
- Any policy or KMS configuration snippets that show export restrictions and KMS roles.

Can you provide the artifacts or point me to where we can review them? Our deadline for the SIG intake is EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Moss
Security Engineer, Acme Corp
security@acme.com

--
From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: Paul Moss <paul.moss@acme.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Proof that wrapped-key exports are non-exportable + wipe logs

Paul — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Irene (crypto ops) and Markus (security attestations). Below is what we can deliver quickly and what we'll need from you if you want deeper telemetry.

What we will deliver by EOD Thursday:
- Signed policy statement (attached: rwf/kms-policy-statement-signed.txt) describing that tenant CEKs are always stored wrapped under a KEK sealed in our HSM and that unwrapped exports require an offline emergency procedure with multi-party authorization (details redacted for ops security).
- Wrapping/rotation logs (attached: rwf/wrapped-key-usage-log-202807.zip) — contains rotation events, wrap key ids, and hashes of wrapped payloads; entries include operator id and M-of-N approval markers where applicable.
- Secure wipe audit (attached: rwf/key-wipe-audit-20280709.pdf) — shows a wipe step following the rotation of ephemeral wrapping keys used during the last tenant onboarding.

If Acme requires deterministic proof that no plaintext export ever occurred (e.g., recorded binary proof for each CEK), we can produce a binding manifest: a CSV with wrapped-key digests + timestamps and a signed statement from our HSM attestation oracle. We can post that to a shared drive or S3; let us know which you prefer.

Irene/Markus, can you confirm the statement on offline emergency export controls and provide the signed attestation blob?

-Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Proof that wrapped-key exports are non-exportable + wipe logs

Chloe, Irene — quick notes for packaging the deliverables to Acme:

1) Attestation: I attached a short signed text block (included in rwf/kms-policy-statement-signed.txt) that enumerates the technical controls — HSM-backed KEK wrapping, no plaintext CEK ejection API, role-based gating with M-of-N emergency process. The attestation references HSM cert serials and the date of the last firmware attestation.

2) Rotation/wipe artifacts: The zip (wrapped-key-usage-log-202807.zip) contains:
   - wrapped-key-manifest.csv (cols: wrapped_key_id, wrapped_digest_sha256, wrap_key_id, timestamp, operator_id)
   - rotation_events.jsonl (human-readable rotation + approval events)
   - wipe_trail.log (audit entries showing wipe command + verification checksums)

3) Confidentiality: The rotation_events.jsonl strips raw CEK material (we never log plaintext CEKs). We can produce a zero-knowledge style proof (HSM-signed digest-of-digests) if Acme needs crypto-binding beyond human-signed attestations.

4) Delivery: I'll place the manifest CSV on our S3 bucket and provide a signed link. Chloe, please coordinate whether Acme wants the Drive link or S3.

I'll also add a short appendix describing the emergency export workflow (process-level, not operational detail) that we can include in the SIG folder.

-Markus
Director, Applied Security, Redwood Inference
From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: Paul Moss <paul.moss@acme.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai

- rwf/wrapped-key-usage-log-202807.zip — manifest + rotation and wipe trails (no plaintext CEKs).
- rwf/key-wipe-audit-20280709.pdf — PDF export of the wipe verification for the last rotation.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the artifacts together.

Regards,
